checks.summary: The secret-free bootstrap and companion-served UI are feasible; real Chrome accepted the exact HttpOnly Secure SameSite=None __Host cookie family in a cross-site loopback iframe, while live Figma remains the frozen release gate.
Official Figma APIs and the closed live capability schema support bounded Frame PNG export, typed Uint8Array transport, and complete same-origin capability loading.
R1 inherits the approved compact and expanded visual contract, all accessibility states, and the frozen Phosphor resolver without new UX discretion.
Initial, manual, and stale pre-insert renders are frozen to exact browser PNG bytes with matching preset identity, metadata, preview, and inserted dimensions.
The canvas mutation is precisely one named image rectangle at source absolute x plus width plus 80 and source y, with result selection, undoability, and source/unrelated-node preservation.
Selection, message, bridge, session, legacy auth, render, image, duplicate, and mutation failure scenarios are concrete and require recoverability with no partial node.
Session issuance/use is restricted by exact route, same origin, client marker, fetch metadata, single auth mode, expiry/restart state, shutdown denial, and no permissive CORS.

The packet excludes bearer/session values from JavaScript-visible state and artifacts; only the required inaccessible HttpOnly cookie and server-side hash/expiry are permitted, with explicit leakage scans and restart invalidation.
Legacy bearer/CORS/shutdown behavior is frozen byte-for-contract while cookie sessions are explicitly denied shutdown and mixed authentication.
The final matrix covers plugin, bridge, security, canvas, visual/accessibility, MCP, mirror, cleanup, and dirty-scope boundaries without remote delivery.
The owned test scopes and exact pattern cover session, same-origin UI, restart invalidation, and selected-Frame behavior.
The existing complete bridge command protects bearer, CORS, preflight, body framing, render, cleanup, and shutdown neighbors.
R1 owns the new plugin tests and package script required to implement the frozen plugin command.
The command is bounded to the two owned implementation surfaces and keeps repository-wide unrelated lint debt outside the gate.
The command covers the sandbox-safe plugin bundles, local manifest/bootstrap, and bridge syntax without generated portfolio dist.
The existing MCP suite is a real frozen regression for the renderer and browser cleanup that remain outside R1 implementation scope.

The observable check makes real Figma Desktop cookie/navigation compatibility, expiry/rotation/restart, legacy parity, shutdown denial, CSRF negatives, and zero manager mutation a mandatory release gate.
The demo is a complete first-value slice from one disposable top-level Frame through exact preview/settings to matching beside-source insertion and one undo.
The check reconciles every live option and representative model/background/layout output at both approved sizes/themes with no stale or unsupported UI.
The check covers every artifact and runtime leakage surface, hashed-session cleanup, four-task security inheritance, legacy parity, mirror/MCP integrity, and dirty-scope isolation.
The frozen icon check requires named imports, typed Question fallback, development-only diagnostics, and excludes placeholders or full-catalog bundling.
The check covers keyboard, focus, names, geometry, announcements, states, reduced motion, themes, approved sizes, and clipping.
R1 ownership is limited to the bridge session extension and new plugin surface; legacy bearer behavior, MCP/mirror, portfolio/dist, publication, delivery, and unrelated dirty work are excluded.
High-risk API expansion is bounded by exact routes, host/origin/fetch metadata, single auth mode, session hash/expiry, shutdown denial, and complete negative tests.
The approved visual gate and Mobbin waiver are inherited without changes, and real Figma accessibility/visual evidence remains mandatory.
Chrome feasibility is proven and exact Figma Desktop cookie/navigation/messaging behavior is an explicit fail-closed release gate rather than an assumed compatibility claim.
No bearer fallback is allowed; raw sessions remain only in HttpOnly cookie transport, server retention is hash-only, leakage scans are comprehensive, and restart invalidates retained cookies.
